jobs.title: Sales Negotiator (full time or part time hours considered)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Friendly and supportive team environment, with great Company benefits including 28 days holiday, birthday paid leave, commission voucher scheme, competitive pay, cycle-2-work scheme, pension, EAP, sick pay, learning and development opportunities, free eye tests and employee discounts! We have been helping people move in Yorkshire for over 200 years. With the advantage of 16 strategically positioned offices, highly trained professionals and enthusiastic marketing teams delivering expert local knowledge - all supported by industry leading technology - you would be right to say we know the region's property market inside out. We are currently recruiting for a Sales Negotiator to join our team in our Knaresborough office on a full time or part time basis (part-time will be considered on a job share basis). The ideal candidate will be responsible for developing close contact with those wishing to buy a property and vendors who want to sell their property, and provide an excellent customer service experience for both potential purchasers' and existing clients'. As a Sales Negotiator you will be responsible for registering new sellers and purchaser details and assessing their needs, assisting in marketing and advertising any properties, dealing with phone and email queries, liaising with all interested parties, negotiate and agree offers to sale agreed, progress sales through to exchange of contracts and completion, and keep administration records updated. This is also a fantastic development opportunity as you will have the chance to develop your skills and knowledge in property valuations. We offer a range of training opportunities, and we encourage our employees to take advantage of these to further their career in the estate agency industry. The individual will need to be hard working, results driven and confident whilst maintaining exceptional customer service. This is a perfect opportunity for someone who has a real interest and proven track record in estate agency and a strong customer service background. At least 1 years experience within the industry is essential and must hold a full driving licence and have access to their own vehicle. If this sounds like it is of interest to you then please don't hesitate and apply or contact us for additional information. Benefits: Company pension Cycle to work scheme Employee discount Health & wellbeing programme Life insurance Sick pay 28 days holiday Birthday Day Off TPBN1_UKTJ

jobs.title: Part-Time Teaching Assistant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Up to £28,437 + Excellent Benefits



Set Working Days: Thursday 8:30 - 16:30 & Friday 8:30 - 16:00



Celebrate the Huge Small Victories

As a Teaching Assistant, you’ll find joy in making even the smallest positive changes in the lives of our young people. We believe in celebrating these "huge small victories" because they add up to create a significant impact. Whether it’s a child sitting through a lesson or engaging with peers, every step forward is worth celebrating!

Curious about what life is like at Witherslack Group? Check out our inspiring video!



Get Out What You Put In

In this role, you’ll work closely with children and young people who have Autistic Spectrum Disorder and Social, Emotional, and Mental Health needs. Your mission? To help them learn, develop their abilities, and boost their self-esteem. While the journey may be challenging, the rewards of witnessing their progress will fill you with pride.

At Witherslack Group, you’ll receive unwavering support from a team of dedicated professionals in well-resourced environments, ensuring you have everything you need to build a fulfilling teaching career.



Join One of the Best Environments in SEND

Hall Cliffe Primary School is an independent specialist day school in Wakefield, dedicated to providing high-quality education for children with a range of special educational needs and disabilities.

Here, you’ll support children who have faced trauma and adversity, many of whom experience Autism, SEMH needs, and high levels of anxiety. As a trauma-informed practitioner, you’ll create a safe space, build trusting relationships, and help them achieve success through creative and adaptive teaching methods.

We’re looking for resilient and compassionate professionals who can foster nurturing environments where children feel valued and ready to learn. This role is challenging yet incredibly rewarding, offering you the chance to make a genuine difference in their lives.



What We Do for You

We recognize your hard work and commitment, and we reward you with one of the best salary and benefits packages in the education sector. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Training: Comprehensive induction and on-the-job training
  • Holiday: Enjoy full school holidays as a reward for your hard work
  • Progression: Opportunities for career development, with many leaders promoted from within
  • Flexible Benefits: Tailor your benefits, including life insurance options
  • Wellbeing: Access to a range of wellbeing tools and employee assistance
  • Medical Cover: Claim back costs for appointments like opticians or dentists
  • Beautiful Work Environments: Work in schools equipped with top-notch facilities
  • Recommend a Friend: Earn a £1,000 bonus for every successful referral
  • Pension: Contributory pension scheme matched up to 5%



Bring Your Whole Self to Work

Our young people come from diverse backgrounds, and we believe our workforce should reflect that diversity. As a Teaching Assistant, you’ll connect with our pupils through:

  • Your ‘can do’ attitude and teamwork spirit
  • Experience in a classroom setting (training provided if needed)
  • A genuine passion for supporting children and making a difference
  • Your enthusiasm to collaborate with teachers and therapists



Interested in Joining Us?

At Witherslack Group, inclusion is at the heart of our mission. We’re dedicated to creating an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and truly belongs.

As a specialist provider of education and care for children with special educational needs, we embrace individuality and champion diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds, identities, and abilities, and we’re committed to making our recruitment and workplace practices inclusive and accessible.

By building a diverse and inclusive team, we enhance our ability to support the children and families we serve, ensuring every member of our team can thrive and be their authentic selves.

The Witherslack Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of its young people. This position is subject to an enhanced DBS check (cost covered) and an online search. We are an equal opportunities employer, welcoming applications from all sections of the community.

For a full job description and person specification, please refer to our resources.

To view our ex-offenders policy, please check our guidelines.

For our Child Protection Policy, please visit the ‘Parents and Carers’ section of our website.
